10.0.0.en: I saw another angel: most interpreters saw that this angel is the Lord Christ Himself in one of the appearances in the Book of Revelation, through the following attributes:

10.0.1.en: Mighty: for He is the owner of all might and authority, indeed their source.

10.0.2.en: Come down from heaven: that is, from His throne and His position in the bosom of the Father.

10.0.3.en: Clothed with a cloud: this is the scene by which Christ described Himself in His Second Coming, "they shall see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory" (Lk 21:27). A rainbow upon his head: this is the same scene we saw around the throne in (ch. 4:3), so it is a scene connected with the glory of Christ.

10.0.4.en: His face was as it were the sun: this is what was said of the Lord Christ Himself at the Transfiguration, "and his face did shine as the sun" (Mt 17:2). And his feet as pillars of fire: the same description of the Lord Christ in (Rev 1:15), meaning feet that are firm and crushing to His enemies.

10.1.0.en: In His appearance He was carrying a little book open, which means that He wants to give us His few words, which nonetheless open the eyes and the heart and give eternal life to whoever acquires them and acts on them. His feet on the sea and on the land: a scene that indicates the comprehensiveness of His effective authority over the earth, the sea and all creation, or as we say in the words of the Divine Liturgy, "the heaven, the earth, the sea and all that is in them ..."

10.2.0.en: He cried with a loud voice: if the sixth trumpet was a symbol of the beginning of the fierce war of the Antichrist and the bearing of very hard woes (ch. 9 ...), the voice of Christ came like the voice of a conquering lion, announcing Himself and giving strength, victory and reassurance to His children amid these hard and terrifying events.

10.2.1.en: When he had cried ... at the end of His mighty voice the seer (St. John) heard the voice of seven thunders. Because thunders are tremendous, frightening sounds, they point to clear and awesome prophecies about the punishment of the wicked.

10.2.2.en: This voice always reaches us in times of hard trials, on the tongues of His faithful children in every age, so that our hope in Him is renewed, or by direct revelations that He permits to us, such as the apparition of the holy Virgin at Zeitoun in 1968, so that the woes have no authority over us ... but His mighty voice comforts our souls in their weakness. Would that when we hear the voice of God supporting us, we draw near to Him and increase in our prayers and readings, so that they may be a fortification for us against any tribulations to come.

10.3.0.en: The task of St. John was to write everything he sees of the various visions throughout this book (ch. 1:19), but when he set about writing what he saw and what he heard of what these seven thunders spoke, the divine command came to him which stopped him from writing what he heard and saw, but to be content with sealing them up. Seal up: an imperative verb meaning close them up, or keep secret what they contain.

10.3.1.en: This command reminds us of what God commanded Daniel also, when He commanded him, saying, "Wherefore shut thou up the vision; for it shall be for many days" (Dan 8:26). And since God did not permit John to write, and therefore did not permit us to know, it is not for us to strive or guess what these thunders contained ... but rather to submit to the wisdom and judgment of God in absolute trust.

10.4.0.en: John returns again to the scene of the angel (Christ) whom he saw, and reminds us of His authority over creation, "standing upon the sea and upon the earth."

10.4.1.en: Lifted up his hand to heaven: as a symbolic reference to God His Father (the hypostasis of the Father), as a preface to what He is about to say. Sware by him that liveth: that is, He called upon the name of the Father as witness, and the expression "sware" is to confirm the decision issued by God, which He is about to announce to us.

10.4.2.en: That there should be time no longer: that is, the end is about to come quickly, and time will not be prolonged after these times and events. Note: a few interpreters, who do not incline to hold that this angel is Christ, also see that the words "sware by him that liveth" do not come from Christ but from an angel who swears by the name of God ... They also say that all the preceding attributes in the description of him in verses (1-3) may belong to an angel of the principalities who took on the splendor of the One who sent him ...

10.4.3.en: We have seen that it is honest to present both interpretations.

10.5.0.en: When the seventh angel is "about" to sound, the appointed time comes that all the faithful servants of God awaited and that He foretold to them in (Mt 24) when He spoke of His Second Coming, and He encouraged the martyrs by their waiting a little season (ch. 6:9-11). What is meant, of course, is the beginning of eternity and the endless reign of Christ.

10.5.1.en: God in His tenderness does not allow hard tribulations to be long, so He brings relief and deliverance quickly, and however many tribulations the days of our life contain, they will be followed by bliss and joy that cannot be expressed. So support us, our God, that we may look to the coming bliss and bear with thanksgiving all that passes over us, and stand firm in our faith and striving to the end.

10.6.0.en: And the voice which I heard from heaven: St. John heard voices from heaven many times, sometimes from Christ Himself as in (chs. 1, 2, 3, 4) and sometimes from angels as in (chs. 5, 6, 7); and so we say here that this voice, which indicates that he had heard it before ... is either a voice from God or the voice of another by His command.

10.6.1.en: Take the little book: the command issued to John was clear, namely to go forward and take this little book and all it contains of prophecies or events from the hand of the angel of whom we spoke in (v. 2).

10.7.0.en: John obeyed and went, and God permitted him to take it, that is, to know it.

10.7.1.en: Eat it up: that is, understand it well, absorb it and discover what it contains of prophecies and events.

10.7.2.en: It shall make thy belly bitter: that is, what you will come to know about some conditions, such as the persecution of the Church or the apostasy and turning away of people from Christ, will grieve your heart and your soul will become pained, "bitter." The meaning may also point to the pains of service that the faithful servant meets in his service.

10.7.3.en: In thy mouth sweet as honey: because preaching in the name of Christ is a joyful work, even if it contains pain and toil. It also means that this little book, though it carries bitter news about the Church and her wars, also contains in it sweet and reassuring revelations about the continuity of Christ's work in her and the proclamation of her final victory.

10.8.0.en: This verse is an explanation of the previous verse, for St. John accomplished what he was commanded and found exactly what he was promised ... It is noted that the expressions the divine inspiration used in these two verses agree completely with what He announced earlier to the prophet Ezekiel in (ch. 3:3, ch. 2:10), for he also ate a book and found in his mouth sweetness as honey, while inside him were "lamentations, and mourning, and woe."

10.9.0.en: God makes clear to John that he must continue in his work of preaching and evangelizing, whatever the bitterness of the soul and the wars of the obstinate. It is a work not limited to a particular people or a specific kingdom but for all people in every age, and it is a work that goes beyond St. John himself to every servant, priest and bishop, so that we care nothing for any toil, nor even for our own souls or their comfort, for the sake of accomplishing what God charges us with.

10.9.1.en: Give us, O God, this fiery heart that knows no discouragement, and if the bitterness in our bellies increases, let us not forget the taste of Your sweet word in our mouths. Strengthen us and help us, and give victory to Your Church and Your flock ... Amen.

10.9.2.en: The two prophets and the resistance to the beast (the Antichrist)

11.0.0.en: A reed like unto a rod: a measure for measuring lengths, like the meter or the yard at the present time. John was given a rod for measuring lengths and was commanded by the angel to measure the temple and the altar, which are the holiest parts of the Jewish temple of old, and also to measure those who worship there, meaning to count their number. Those who worship are the children of God who worship Him in His Church, and their most important feature is humility.

11.1.0.en: The court which is without: it was the outer part of the Jewish temple and was not as important as the place of the altar referred to in the previous verse. As for the spiritual meaning, the angel commanded St. John not to measure the outer part, that is, those outside the faith (the Gentiles), defiled by their sins and their evil thoughts, who become a cause of defilement and stumbling for the world that God wants to be holy to Him, "the holy city." Their stumbling continues for forty-two months, which is the period of the Antichrist's dominion and his evils. The three and a half years are half of seven, the number that symbolizes perfection, and so we can say that it is a period that will not be very long. No one can affirm whether this is a real time or a symbolic, prophetic time.

11.1.1.en: God feels for you in the midst of your tribulations. You are one of His children; He cares for you and for your relationship with His Church, and He keeps the wicked away from you however much they surround you. He also does not allow the tribulation to be long, but supports you until you come out of it and enjoy His blessings and heavenly glories.

11.2.s.en: (2) The sending of the two prophets

11.2.0.en: Since the period of the dominion of evil, that is, of the Antichrist, is three and a half years, God sends a special and very powerful grace, namely two witnesses (prophets) who prophesy and support the Church during the same period, for the one thousand two hundred and sixty days are the same as the time of three and a half years (considering the Jewish year to be 360 days). My two witnesses: the Orthodox Church sees in the interpretations of her Fathers that these two witnesses are "Elijah and Enoch," since neither of them died but were taken up to heaven, and they will taste bodily death in (v. 8), as will come.

11.2.1.en: Clothed in sackcloth: a sign of their grief at what the state of things on earth has come to, and what has befallen many of the believers, and the severity of the war of the beast (the Antichrist).

11.3.0.en: The two olive trees and the two candlesticks: a description of the two prophets. The olive signifies peace, safety and life, just as the dove came in the days of Noah carrying an olive branch as a sign of the end of the Flood, and likewise the lampstand signifies the Church, witnessing to her Christ by the lights of her teaching.

11.3.1.en: Before the Lord: that is, everything they speak is for the Lord, its source is the Lord, and it is with the blessing and support of God. They will not flatter anyone, for their teaching is frank, pure and clear.

11.3.2.en: Give me, O God, the spirit of Elijah and Enoch, that I may witness to Your name and proclaim Your truth, so that Your commandment may be raised and exalted above the blasphemy of the world, and do not let me fear or be afraid of anything except Your wrath ... Help me, Lord, for I am weak.

11.4.0.en: The Lord gave them authority for the whole time of their ministry on earth, and this authority is referred to by fire coming out of their mouth, because the words that come out of their mouths consume every false teaching or doubt from Satan and his helpers ... The expression of fire coming out of their words reminds us of what actually happened between Elijah and the messenger of King Ahaziah when Elijah rebuked him, "and there came down fire from heaven, and consumed him and his fifty" (2 Kgs 1:

11.4.1.en: 1-12.) No one can approach them, for whoever approaches them, his end is destruction.

11.5.0.en: Part of the strength of their authority is also that God gave them authority to shut heaven, that is, to withhold its goods, and this also reminds us of what Elijah did in shutting heaven from rain for three and a half years (1 Kgs 17:1) in the days of the wicked King Ahab. They also have the authority and power of God that He gave to Moses when he turned the waters of the Nile into blood (Ex 7:20). The overall meaning of the two verses (5, 6) is that God gave them authority and power exceeding every power of men, to do what they wish upon the whole face of the earth.

11.5.1.en: Does this not remind us, beloved, of the authority God deposited in His Church for the forgiveness of the sins of the penitent through the sacrament of the priesthood and the sacrament of confession, when He said to His pure Apostles, "Whatsoever ye shall bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever ye shall loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven" (Mt 18:18)? So seize this opportunity, my brother, and enjoy this authority, that you may obtain God's forgiveness and a place in heaven.

11.6.0.en: When they shall have finished their testimony: that is, the end of the period set by God for their coming down, their resistance to Satan and their witness.

11.6.1.en: The beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit: Satan himself with all his power and authority, and the abyss, that is, Hades, is the place of his kingdom and authority and a clear indication of his nature.

11.6.2.en: Shall make war against them, and shall overcome them: after Satan saw what these two prophets did, it was given to him, by God's permission, to gather all the forces of evil and be able to kill the two prophets, but his authority is limited, for it is over bodies only and not spirits. Let us remember the saying of our Lord, "Fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul" (Mt 10:28).

11.7.0.en: The great city: great in the eyes of evil and the wicked because it symbolizes the authority of Satan and his works in it.

11.7.1.en: Which spiritually is called: resembles or symbolizes.

11.7.2.en: Sodom and Egypt: Sodom and Egypt of old symbolized the wicked pagan kingdoms that resisted God. Where also our Lord was crucified: of course Christ was crucified in Jerusalem, but because the meaning is spiritual, what is meant by the general sense of the verse is that the evil latent in the world that rejects God, which by its evil crucified the Lord of glory, believing it had triumphed over Him, is the very same evil that killed these two prophets.

11.8.0.en: The wicked gather from every direction, nation and place to gaze, without pity but with every gloating, at the state of these two prophets after their death, as though evil wants to satisfy its rage against these two witnesses who troubled it throughout the former time. From the excess of evil's cruelty, it left the corpses and did not bury them for three and a half days, and this period may be real time or figurative ... but it is a short time.

11.8.1.en: Among the displays of gloating ... is that the kingdom of evil, with all its members, congratulate one another on the killing of the two prophets and send gifts, as though what happened were a feast and a victory for them.

11.8.2.en: Because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth: the reason and cause of the joy of the evil world is that it has been relieved of the rebuke, reproof and warnings that the two prophets carried to them, and also of some of the blows they brought down on the world because of its evil (v. 6).

11.8.3.en: So it is with the wicked in every age. Instead of responding to the warnings of God and His disciplines that He sends through the mouth of His saints and faithful servants, the wicked often want to be rid of them because they alert people and try to turn them away from the way of Satan, as happened with St. John the Baptist, St. John Chrysostom and Pope Athanasius the Apostolic. I beg You, my God, make my heart always obedient to Your voice and submissive to it ... and remove from it all hardness, refusal and stubbornness.

11.9.0.en: After the short joy that the wicked enjoyed in their gloating (three and a half days), God restored them to life by His power and in a miraculous way. Just as His glorious Resurrection was an earthquake to the whole kingdom of evil, so also the resurrection of the two witnessing prophets caused great fear and terror among the pillars of the wicked world, which had been arrogantly contemplating its false victory over them.

11.10.0.en: They heard a great voice from heaven: God, who honors His faithful holy children, proclaims His honoring of them by calling to them to ascend to heaven, and they ascended to heaven after the pattern of the ascension of the Lord Himself in a cloud (Acts 1:9). As the disciples saw the ascension of Christ, the wicked enemies saw their ascension, so it was a victory and a crown for the two prophets and shame and disgrace for the kingdom of evil.

11.10.1.en: I thank You, Lord, because even if evil triumphs for a time, its end is known, and even if it seems to us that it has authority over Your children, Your strong hand gives them resurrection, glory, honor and a proclamation of their holiness even after their death, as happened with many of the holy martyrs.

11.11.0.en: The same hour: that is, the moment of the ascension of the two witnesses to heaven.

11.11.1.en: A great earthquake: a figure for the proclamation of the wrath and anger of God on the wicked and the beast.

11.11.2.en: The tenth part of the city: that is, this was a relative vengeance from God, but the general judgment has not yet come. At the ascension of the witnesses to heaven God shows something of His wrath on the kingdom of evil, so a great earthquake occurs that shakes its pillars and foundations, and a tenth of the wicked people fall, whom St. John estimates at seven thousand. The number here is of course symbolic and means relative multitude, since seven and a thousand are numbers of perfection. Names of men: this means that God in His just judgment knows exactly to whom He directs His blow, as though this vengeance were directed to people known by name to God.

11.11.3.en: Gave glory: the fear and terror that seized the wicked wrung from them a confession of the power of the God of these two witnesses, so they offered Him glorification and knew that He is the true God.

11.12.0.en: The first woe was the blow of the locusts (ch. 8:13), and the second woe carried the blow of the armies of horsemen (ch. 9:12) and also the blows of the two witnessing prophets. With the end of their story the inspired text announces the end of the second woe, but it alerts us to the existence of a third woe.

11.13.0.en: The talk about the angel of the sixth trumpet ended at the end of chapter nine, and chapter ten and chapter eleven up to the previous verse contained interjected events, and we now return to the seventh angel and the last trumpet.

11.13.1.en: When the seventh angel sounded, a proclamation was made in heaven with great jubilation, in which all the heavenly creation took part, of the end of the events and the wrathful, disciplining blows. Now has come the proclamation of the final victory over the kingdom of evil, and the whole world has become subject to the authority of God the Father and His only-begotten Son, who announced with voices of glorification the beginning of His endless reign.

11.13.2.en: Vv. 16, 17 The four: and twenty priests: (see ch. 4:4).

11.13.3.en: Fell upon their faces and worshipped: the twenty-four priests, as they did before (ch. 4:10), offering praise, thanksgiving and honor. This time the subject of their praise was the offering of thanks for the work of God in punishing the kingdom of evil and refuting it, in spreading His reign, in the return of the world to faith, and in the proclamation of God's infinite power in making and ordering all this.

11.13.4.en: Thou hast taken to thee thy great power: that is, it was always Yours, but You proclaimed it at the appropriate time.

11.14.0.en: The wicked nations were angry and Your Church suffered for a time because of them, but the anger of the nations is counted as nothing before You, for Your wrath is what everyone should fear, and it is what has happened and indeed come. The time of the dead: that is, the time of the wicked and their judgment.

11.14.1.en: Thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants: that is, the recompense and the inheritance of the Kingdom.

11.14.3.en: The prophets: that is, those who witnessed and served the word of God and conveyed it and interpreted it to people.

11.14.4.en: The saints: everyone who walked in the fear of God, trying to please Him by carrying out His commandments.

11.14.5.en: Them that fear thy name: everyone who set the fear of God before him so as not to sin.

11.14.6.en: Small and great: that is, all who followed You, whatever their standing or age.

11.14.7.en: As for those who wearied the earth and destroyed many by their evils, they will receive the like of what they did, that is, God's justice requires their eternal destruction.

11.15.0.en: The temple of God was opened in heaven: that is, the perfect glory of God in eternity was proclaimed, and it means the entrance of the righteous believers to enjoy eternal existence with Him.

11.15.1.en: There was seen in his temple the ark of his testament: the ark of the covenant always symbolized the continual presence of God in the midst of His people, and the appearance of the ark of the covenant here means confirmation of the opening of the temple and everyone's enjoyment of this presence and constant standing before God.

11.15.2.en: There were lightnings, and voices, and thunderings, and an earthquake, and great hail: in this part of the verse there are two meanings. The first makes clear that being in the divine presence is an awesome presence, for all these phenomena are connected with the divine glory. The second meaning is that the temple of God, in which His children enjoy being with Him, is itself the source of His justice, and from it come His judgments and punishments for the wicked, and this agrees with the word "hail," since whenever it appears in the Holy Bible it mostly carries the meaning of punishment.

11.15.3.en: My God, how beautiful it is to be with You and to enjoy You in Your heavenly temple ... and You have also granted us to stand in Your holy temple in Your Church here, so that we are counted as those standing in heaven, as though we are receiving a pledge of the everlasting eternal glory ... Make us worthy, my Lord, to complete the days of our bodily sojourn in Your fear and Your favor, that we may enjoy what You prepared for us before the foundation of the world.

11.15.4.en: Satan resists the Church, a general introduction: the second and thirteenth chapters include a scene picturing the Church and her wars with Satan in three images: the first with the dragon, whose origin was from heaven; the second with a beast coming up out of the sea; and the third with a beast coming up out of the earth. The general meaning of the two chapters is that Satan's war against the Church is a perpetual war from her birth and in every place.
